uncited: Elongation is a domain manipulation operator for Signed Distance Fields (SDFs) that stretches a shape along a specified vector.
It solves the problem of creating tapered or extended geometric forms from base primitives without altering the primitive's core definition.

It is distinct from [SDF Domain Manipulation Operators](1730-sdf-domain-manipulation-operators.md) in that it specifically modifies the distance value based on a directional vector rather than just transforming the input coordinates, and from [SDF Primitives](1731-sdf-primitives.md) as it is a post-processing step applied to an existing SDF evaluation.
- Intermediate vectors $q$ and scalar $d$.
Evaluate the base SDF at the positive part of $q$.
Let $q_+$ be the component-wise positive part of $q$ (i.e., $q_+ = \max(q, 0)$).
Add the maximum component of $q_-$ to the base distance.
Its magnitude controls the degree of stretch.
Direction determines the axis of elongation.
- If $s$ is zero, the operator returns the base SDF evaluated at $|p|$.
- Precision issues may arise if $|p|$ and $s$ are very close, leading to cancellation errors in $q$.
- The base SDF must handle the transformed coordinates correctly; if the base SDF assumes a specific orientation, the elongation vector must align with it.
A technique to address field variation divergence near skeleton end-points in SCALIS fields.
It forces an additional sampling position near end-points to increase correlation between the minima of individual primitives and the global field.
It is implemented by adding a segment primitive with constant radius at the end vertices of the skeleton.
The length of the end-point corrector segment is proportional to the prescribed radius at the end vertices of the skeleton and a constant depending on the kernel used.
- Scales linearly with the complexity of the base SDF.
- Limitations: The resulting SDF may not be perfectly smooth if the base SDF has discontinuities or if the elongation vector causes self-intersections in the distance field logic.
- Use when you need to stretch or taper a shape along a specific axis.

- Do not use when you need a perfectly smooth, continuous distance field without any potential artifacts from the max operation, or when the base primitive is not suitable for the elongation direction.
